comments.content: This mutates the input `mpi` in place via `mp_image_vflip(mpi)`. `mpi` may be a reference to a frame owned by the decoder or another filter, and flipping it in place corrupts the shared image data (and its params) for any other consumer. It also permanently clears `params.vflip` on the shared image. Consider flipping a copy (e.g. `mp_image_new_ref` + flip, or flipping only the upload path) instead of modifying the caller's frame.

`layout.params.vflip` is used to set `.flipped` on the plane, but `layout` is derived from the image before the in-place `mp_image_vflip()` below. Since the flip is applied later in the same function, the plane `flipped` flag and the actual flipped data may be inconsistent (double-flip or no flip). Verify the ordering: either set `.flipped` based on the post-flip state, or don't flip the image and rely solely on `.flipped`.

`p->target_vflip` is set to `vflip` (the current image's vflip) before the early-return checks. If the VO supports vflip (`info->vflip`), the code returns without inserting a filter, but `p->target_vflip` remains equal to the input vflip. On the next frame with the same vflip/imgfmt, the fast path sets `img->params.vflip = p->target_vflip` (unchanged), which is fine, but if the VO capability changes or the filter is later inserted, the stale `target_vflip` may not reflect the intended output. More importantly, when a vflip filter *is* inserted, `target_vflip` is set to 0, but `prev_vflip` still holds the original value; the fast-path condition compares `img->params.vflip == p->prev_vflip`, so a subsequent frame with the same input vflip will take the fast path and set `vflip = 0` — correct. However, if the input vflip toggles back, the drain/destroy path re-runs and re-inserts the filter. This logic appears intentional but is fragile; consider documenting the invariant or resetting `prev_vflip`/`prev_imgfmt` when the filter is destroyed.

`img->params.rotate / 90 + 4 * !!img->params.vflip` — the `wl_surface_set_buffer_transform` enum values are 0..7 (WL_OUTPUT_TRANSFORM_NORMAL..FLIPPED_ROTATED_270). Adding 4 maps rotate 0/90/180/270 to flipped variants 4/5/6/7, which is correct for the Wayland enum ordering. However, `img->params.rotate` is not guaranteed to be a multiple of 90 here (the autorotate filter normally normalizes it, but this VO may receive unnormalized values). Consider masking with `% 360` and asserting the multiple-of-90 invariant.

The determinant is computed from `matrix[0..4]` as a 3x3 display matrix (indices 0,1,3,4). This is correct for the AV_FRAME_DATA_DISPLAYMATRIX layout, but `sd->data` size is not validated. If the side data is malformed/short, reading `matrix[4]` is out of bounds. Consider checking `sd->size >= 9 * sizeof(int32_t)` before dereferencing.

`pars->distort_params.transform.mat` is set only when `vflip` is true, but `params.distort_params` is not reset to NULL when `vflip` is false on a subsequent frame. If `pars` persists across frames, a previously-set transform will leak into frames that should not be flipped. Ensure `params.distort_params = NULL` (or reset the matrix) in the else branch.
